title: NFL Playoff Picture 2026: Week 12 AFC & NFC Standings, Brackets & Tiebreakers Updated【NBC Sports】
body:
The Thanksgiving weekend turned into a high‑stakes marathon for the NFL, with nine of the ten teams on the field seeing their playoff hopes either surge or slip as the league entered Week 12. While the Philadelphia Eagles, already eliminated, staged a dramatic comeback to beat the Dallas Cowboys in a game that reminded fans why football is still the sport of miracles, the real story unfolded in the conference standings, where a single win or loss reshaped the AFC and NFC brackets and forced the league into a cascade of tiebreaker calculations.

In the AFC, the Buffalo Bills solidified their grip on the top seed with a decisive victory over the New England Patriots, pushing them to a 9‑2 record and guaranteeing home‑field advantage throughout the postseason. Behind them, the Kansas City Chiefs, who entered the week tied with the Bills, fell to 8‑3 after a narrow loss to the Indianapolis Colts, dropping them to the second seed. The Miami Dolphins, riding a three‑game winning streak, climbed to 7‑4 and now sit in the third spot, while the Baltimore Ravens, despite a loss to the Steelers, remain in contention for a wild‑card berth at 6‑5 thanks to a favorable conference record. The AFC’s bottom half is a tangle of teams with identical records—Cincinnati, Cleveland, and the Los Angeles Chargers—all sitting at 5‑6, meaning head‑to‑head results and division records will determine who clings to the final wild‑card slot.

The NFC saw even more turbulence. The Dallas Cowboys, buoyed by a late‑quarter rally against the Eagles, improved to 8‑3 and reclaimed the division lead, edging out the San Francisco 49ers, who slipped to 7‑4 after a loss to the Seattle Seahawks. The Seattle club, now 7‑4, holds the second seed thanks to a superior divisional record, while the New York Giants, fresh off a surprise win over the Washington Commanders, rose to 6‑5 and are now firmly in the wild‑card conversation. The Los Angeles Rams, who entered the week at 5‑6, fell to 5‑7 after a defeat by the Arizona Cardinals, leaving them on the outside looking in. Meanwhile, the Chicago Bears and the Philadelphia Eagles, both at 4‑7, are mathematically eliminated, but the Bears remain in the conversation for a potential “play‑in” scenario should the league adopt a new format next season.

Tiebreakers have already begun to dominate front‑office discussions. In the AFC, the Bills and Chiefs will rely on their head‑to‑head record—Kansas City leads the series 2‑1—should they finish with identical win totals, but the Bills’ superior conference record (7‑1 versus 6‑2) gives them the edge if the tie extends beyond the first criterion. The Ravens, tied with the Chargers at 6‑5, will look to their division record (3‑3 versus 2‑4) to stay alive, while the Chargers hope a victory over the Denver Broncos will swing the head‑to‑head tiebreaker in their favor. In the NFC, the Cowboys and 49ers are separated by a single division win; Dallas holds a 2‑1 edge, but San Francisco’s better overall conference record could become decisive if both teams finish 9‑3. Seattle’s wild‑card chances hinge on its 5‑2 conference record, which currently outpaces the Giants’ 4‑3, meaning a loss could drop the Giants into a three‑team tie that would be settled by net points in games among the tied clubs.

The Thanksgiving games themselves provided a microcosm of the season’s narrative. Dallas’ comeback against a winless Philadelphia highlighted the resilience of a team that, despite early‑season injuries, has learned to thrive under pressure. Meanwhile, the Detroit Lions’ overtime triumph over the Green Bay Packers kept the Lions alive for a wild‑card spot, while the Chicago Bears’ loss to the Vikings effectively ended their postseason hopes. The collective impact of these five contests was a net shift of three playoff positions across the two conferences, underscoring how a single weekend can accelerate or halt a franchise’s trajectory.

Looking ahead, Week 13 will be a make‑or‑break stretch for several clubs teetering on the edge of the postseason. Buffalo and Dallas will aim to cement their top‑seed status, while teams like Baltimore, Seattle, and Miami must secure victories to avoid being swallowed by the tiebreaker maelstrom. The league’s remaining schedule still offers ample opportunity for surprise upsets, but the Thanksgiving results have already narrowed the field and set the stage for a dramatic sprint to the playoffs.
